content:
OSKAR HADDAD-LINDQVIST
Full-Stack Developer | TypeScript, React and Node.js

oskar.hl@example.com | +46 70 555 0808
GitHub: github.com/oskarhl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional web development experience and a particular strength in frontend engineering. Builds customer-facing applications with React, TypeScript, Node.js and SQL, with experience spanning accessibility, mobile performance, identity verification and automated testing. Experienced in cross-functional product teams and mentoring.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | 2021–Present
- Build customer onboarding and KYC flows in a six-person team using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL.
- Built a BankID identity verification flow using a provider SDK, including QR code and same-device flows, error handling and retries. A/B tested the flow on 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
- Built a document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in AWS Lambda, and scan status updates through SQS and PostgreSQL.
- Improved mobile Largest Contentful Paint from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds through code splitting, image optimisation and dependency changes. Used Next.js server-side rendering for landing pages.
- Addressed WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit findings in the onboarding flow and migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite.
- Helped migrate the backend incrementally from Express to NestJS and maintains a GraphQL BFF with another developer.
- Worked with designers in Figma, supported production through an on-call rotation and interviewed candidates. Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024, conducting 1:1s and sprint planning.
- The onboarding team received an internal customer impact award in 2023.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | 2018–2021
- Built websites and web applications for approximately 25 clients using React, Angular, Node.js, Express, PHP and Laravel.
- Served as project tech lead on a two-developer React Native ferry ticket app, building most of the app, including ticket purchase and offline display. The app reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Set up GitLab CI for the agency and developed custom WordPress themes and plugins.

Web Developer | Nordkust Media AB | 2014–2018
- Developed newspaper websites using PHP, jQuery and MySQL, and worked on an AngularJS article editor.
- Built a paywall integration and contributed to Varnish caching configuration and Ubuntu server administration.

Freelance Web Developer / Student | 2012–2014
- Built websites for individuals, a local bakery and two bands using PHP, jQuery and WordPress.

SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Next.js, Angular, React Native, Storybook
Backend and databases: Node.js, NestJS, Express, REST, GraphQL, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Prisma
Testing and workflows: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI
Cloud and operations: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS and CloudWatch; Docker; Linux
Other: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility audit fixes, A/B testing, Figma, Unleash, Agile/Scrum, BankID

EDUCATION
Bachelor in Computer Science | West Coast University College (Högskola) | 2011–2014

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
- Mentor, coding bootcamp | 2019–2020
- Speaker, local JavaScript meetup | 2022: “Migrating Express to NestJS without stopping the world”

LANGUAGES
Swedish: native | English: fluent | Arabic: spoken

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured, professionally presented CV with clear role targeting for a Full-Stack Engineer focused on TypeScript and React. The summary is concise and relevant, the experience section uses strong technical detail, and the quantified outcomes—onboarding conversion increasing from 61% to 74%, mobile LCP improving from 4.1 to 1.9 seconds, and approximately 50,000 app downloads—provide credible impact. The progression from web developer to full-stack developer is clear, and leadership, mentoring, design collaboration, accessibility, and production support are all relevant to the role. The main content weakness is that some relevant capabilities are listed only in the Skills section rather than demonstrated in the experience bullets, particularly automated testing and Git-based workflows.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain-text formatting, readable bullets, and relevant keyword coverage including React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, SQL-related databases, WCAG, Jest, Playwright, AWS, Docker, Storybook, Next.js, and A/B testing. It should perform well in both conventional ATS parsing and AI-based screening, with a high estimated screening probability because the core must-have technologies and experience are clearly visible. Minor keyword opportunities remain: the document does not explicitly use the phrases "Git-based workflows," "unit testing," "end-to-end testing," "semantic HTML," or "responsive layouts." These concepts should only be made more explicit where they accurately describe the candidate's existing experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is an excellent match for the core role. It clearly demonstrates substantially more than two years of professional React and TypeScript experience; Node.js backend development; PostgreSQL and other SQL databases; accessibility work; automated testing tools; AWS and Docker; Next.js server-side rendering; Storybook; A/B testing; cross-functional collaboration; sprint planning; mentoring; and fluent English. The fintech KYC, BankID identity verification, and secure document-upload work provide relevant experience in a regulated and security-sensitive environment, although it is not healthcare experience specifically. The strongest remaining alignment gaps are explicit evidence of semantic HTML and responsive layouts, explicit awareness of OWASP/web-security fundamentals, and a stated willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. German is listed in the source material as mostly forgotten at school level, and no Croatian is documented, so the German/Croatian nice-to-have is not met. These are job-fit gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ATS AND EVIDENCE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Skills section, change "Testing and workflows: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI" to "Automated testing and Git-based workflows: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI." This makes the existing evidence match the job description's terminology without adding a new skill.
2. In the Skills section, change "Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Next.js..." to "Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, semantic HTML, CSS, responsive web development, Next.js..." only if the candidate is comfortable that their existing HTML/CSS and mobile-performance work represent semantic HTML and responsive web development. These terms are supported by the source material's HTML/CSS experience and mobile optimization, but should not be retained if they would overstate the experience.
3. In the Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, add a short testing/workflow bullet only if accurate, such as: "Develop and maintain automated frontend and backend tests using Jest and Playwright within GitHub Actions workflows." The original candidate information lists these tools and GitHub Actions, but the current CV does not show how they were used in practice. Do not add this sentence if the tools were only used by other team members.
4. In the Experience section under Älvgrind Fintech AB, make the security relevance more explicit without claiming OWASP expertise. For example, revise the document-upload bullet to: "Built a secure document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in AWS Lambda, and scan-status updates through SQS and PostgreSQL." This accurately highlights the existing security-related work.
